blocks.text: Intro
narrow mono. Fingerpicked acoustic guitar and stubborn upright bass. Two distant accordion notes interrupt, like a phone ringing. Close-mic female contralto, almost spoken.

Feels like a rash this week
Right under the skin
Nothing catastrophic
Just the itch again
Verse 1
brushed snare slips in; bass stays patient. Scratchy guitar fills the gaps. Accordion's two-note call interrupts but never wins.

Headlines falling like sparks on oil
Every feed another flame
Leaks and counter-leaks and shouting mouths
All begging for a name

Your finger hovers over send
Your pulse begins to pitch
Funny how the loudest world
Just keeps on asking you to itch
Pre-Chorus
groove tightens, not louder. Dry guitar scratches against the snare.

Scratch it once
The rash will spread
Scratch it twice
It's in your head
Chorus
full band drops out for the title, voice alone. One beat of silence follows "call." Scrappy swing returns with restrained boot stomp and handclaps. No belting.
Refuse the call

Let it ring, let it ring
Not every war that finds your door
Deserves the breath you bring
Accordion answers with the two-note call. Bass ignores it.

Stay off the wire
Let the static fade
Some storms collapse
When they're not obeyed
Band cuts again. Singer stays calm.
Refuse the call

Let the shouting pass you by
Sometimes the bravest thing to do
Is let the signal die
Verse 2
percussion backs away. Accordion becomes a wheedling carnival barker. Vocal is amused, not angry.

There's a barker on the midway
Calling out your name
Got a wheel that only turns
For the ones who play his game

You can stroll right past the booth
Let him holler, let him try
He can shout till morning comes
You don't owe him a reply
Pre-Chorus
accordion call grows insistent. Bass never changes pace.

He needs your eyes
He needs your ear
The wheel speeds up
When you draw near
Chorus
junk percussion makes the machinery busier. Vocal gets quieter and firmer. Full-band dropout on the title.
Refuse the call

Let it ring, let it ring
Not every war that finds your door
Deserves the breath you bring

Stay off the wire
Let the static fade
Some storms collapse
When they're not obeyed
Refuse the call

Let the shouting pass you by
Sometimes the bravest thing to do
Is let the signal die
Bridge
HARD DROPOUT. Voice and upright bass, nearly silence. Accordion attempts its two-note call once and is cut off. No swell.

You can hear the engines grinding
Every platform wants a fight
Every spark demands a witness
Every rumor needs a light

But there's work beyond the midway
Past the last electric flame
Something small that needs your hands
And doesn't even ask your name
Two boot stomps. Uneven handclaps enter. Bass continues, completely undisturbed.
Final Chorus
roughest groove, not loudest. Claps and junk percussion press forward. Singer sits behind the beat, almost whispering. Hard instrumental cut after the title.
Refuse the call

Let it ring against the wall
A voice without an answer
Is a voice, and that is all

Stay off the wire
Let the static fade
Some storms collapse
When they're not obeyed
Outro
guitar, drums and claps drop out one by one. The accordion calls twice into the empty room.

The wheel still turns
The last bulb burns
The barker calls into the dark
Two-note accordion call. Long empty pause.
No answer.
Complete silence. Spoken, dry, almost an afterthought.
No next mark.

notebook.style: Dark folk-noir cabaret, crooked small-band swing, ~96 BPM; urgent feet, unhurried voice, Low, weathered female contralto, chesty and close, dry talk-sung phrasing, wry and resolute; never belting, Mono opening: fingerpicked acoustic guitar and stubborn upright bass ostinato, Brushed snare and muted kick slip into a loping pocket, Accordion plays a nagging two-note “call” motif, returning between phrases and growing pushier without getting louder, Guitar answers in scratchy little “itch” figures; junk percussion, boot stomps and ragged handclaps mimic carnival machinery, Each “Refuse the call” lands on two hard stresses, followed by a razor-cut band silence before the groove resumes, Bass stays steady while everything else fusses, Dry room mics, tape grit, narrow-to-wide mix; no gloss, choirs or vocal runs, Bridge: almost just voice and bass, Final chorus rougher and rhythmically insistent, not triumphant, Instruments peel away; unanswered accordion figure, then true silence
